Plan 1: One-pan lemon‑herb chicken with roasted veggies + quick couscous (serves 4)
Why it works: mostly hands-off once it’s in the oven, uses simple ingredients, and gives you a complete meal with protein, veggies, and a grain.

What you’ll need (approximate quantities)
- 4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts (about 1 to 1.2 lb)
- 2 cups mixed veg (like broccoli florets, bell pepper strips, and carrot sticks)
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano or Italian seasoning
- Salt and pepper
- 1 cup couscous (or quinoa) and 1 cup water or chicken broth
- Optional quick yogurt-lemon sauce: 1/2 cup plain yogurt, a squeeze of lemon, pinch of salt
- Optional parsley for garnish

Simple steps
1) Heat oven to 425°F (220°C).
2) Toss chicken with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the lemon zest, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
3) Toss veggies with the remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper.
4) Spread chicken on a sheet pan and surround with veggies. Bake 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and veggies are tender.
5) While that bakes, make couscous: bring 1 cup water or broth to a boil, stir in couscous, cover 5 minutes, fluff.
6) Mix a quick sauce if you like: yogurt with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
7) Serve chicken and veggies over couscous. Garnish with a little parsley if you have it.

Time estimate: about 40–45 minutes total. Minimal cleanup.

Backup easy options (if you’d rather do something different)
- Taco bowl night (quick and fun): Sauté lean ground turkey or beef with mild taco seasoning; serve with brown rice or quinoa, lettuce, tomato, avocado, cheese, and salsa. Time ~25–30 minutes.
- Pita pizzas: Whole-wheat pitas, pizza sauce, mozzarella, and healthy toppings (veggies, olives, leftover chicken). Bake at 425°F for 8–10 minutes. Time ~15–20 minutes.
- Salmon foil packs: 4 small salmon fillets with lemon, dill, and some green beans or asparagus in foil packets. Bake 15–20 minutes. Time ~25–30 minutes.

Tips to make it easier
- Do a little prep ahead: chop veggies the night before or the morning of, and you can even mix the marinade for the chicken ahead of time.
- Buy pre-cut veggies or a bag of salad mix to cut down prep.
- Let the kids help with toppings or setting the table; it makes them comfortable with the meal.
- If you want a “fridge-to-oven” plan, you could marinate the chicken in the morning and pull it out right before cooking.
